title: field-guide-session-segmentation-and-observability-experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact field guide for running small observability experiments focused on session segmentation (how we group related token requests), metric contracts for those segments, and trace/ dashboard patterns that make investigation fast and low-cost. Intended audience: oncall engineers, product SREs, and feature owners planning rollout probes.

Context & why this matters:
- Multi-hop chat and long-context inference create scattered telemetry: prefix cache hits, KV eviction, fanout to alignment and moderation models.
- Investigations are slow because operators must reconstruct sessions across services (API gateway -> router -> runtime -> model-sidecar).
- We want cheap, high-signal probes and dashboard panels that localize blame quickly while minimizing query cost.

Experiment goals (small, timeboxed):
1) Define a session key that is stable across a user flow (session_id + seq_number).
2) Attach 1 lightweight session-level metric (session_latency_ms_p50/p95) and 2 event metrics (kvcache_hit_rate, model_fanout_count).
3) Instrument a single trace-span anchor at Router->Runtime boundary with session tags to link traces to metric rollups.
4) Build a compact dashboard tile set that supports 3 common triage flows (latency spike, cost spike, hallucination report).

Minimal metric definitions (contract-ready):
- session_latency_ms_p50: p50 of end_to_end_latency_ms aggregated by session window (30s sliding). Unit: ms. Owner: eng-observability. Alert if p95(session_latency_ms) increases by >25% over baseline for 15m.
- session_token_count: count of request tokens per session (sum). Taggable by model, region, plan. Use for cost attribution.
- kvcache_hit_rate: ratio of requests with KV cache hit / total requests, rollup by session and model. Owner: serving-runtime team. Note: sample at 1/10 for high volume models.
- model_fanout_count: integer number of backend model calls per request (0..n). Helps detect inadvertent cascade to heavy models.

Tracing & span guidelines (cheap & high-utility):
- Span of interest: Router->Runtime handoff. Name: router.runtime.handoff.
- Required attributes: session_id (string), session_seq (int), model_variant (string), tenant_id (string), kv_hit:boolean. Keep attribute names stable.
- Sampling: anchor trace sampling to sessions that hit either high latency or kvcache_miss AND model_fanout_count>1. This hybrid ensures we capture problematic flows without blowing budget.
- Trace length: aim for 3-6 spans for quick visualization. Avoid auto-capturing large model payloads; instead include payload digests only (sha1).

Dashboard tile set (compact template):
- Tile A (Operator summary): p95 session latency (last 1h/24h), session count, token throughput. One-line health status.
- Tile B (Cache warmth): kvcache_hit_rate by model (top 10) with trendline.
- Tile C (Fanout map): histogram of model_fanout_count and sample error rates per fanout depth.
- Tile D (Session explorer): searchable table for session_id, start_time, session_latency_ms_p95, kv_hit_rate, linked trace id (clickable). Limit to 500 rows; default time range 1h.
- Cost control: every dashboard query must include a cost cap flag; prefer pre-aggregated metrics (session-level) rather than raw event scans.

Investigation playflows (quick recipes):
- Latency spike: open Tile A -> identify top sessions -> click session_id -> open linked trace -> check kv_hit, model_fanout_count -> if kvcache_miss correlated, file ticket against serving-runtime with examples (attach 3 traces).
- Cost spike: Tile B + C -> if fanout_count increases, check rollout flags/gradual releases.
- Output quality: correlate small eval prompt set (external) with session_token_count and model_variant, watch for regression windows.

Open questions & proposed experiments:
- Session key design: should we use client-generated session_id or canonicalize server-side? Trade-offs: client respects user boundaries but is noisy. Proposal: fallback to server-canonical when missing. (Experiment A / JIRA-6721)
- Trace retention tiers: capture anchor traces at full fidelity for 7d, light digests for 30d. Cost estimate needed from observability-cost team.
- Adaptive sampling policy: test hybrid rule for 2 weeks on a 10% traffic slice. Measure signal/noise ratio (operator time-to-root-cause).

Immediate next steps (this sprint):
- [ ] Add session_id/session_seq tags to router-runtime handoff span (PR: obs-infra #487). Owner: Elliot. ETA: 2026-03-05.
- [ ] Create pre-aggregated session metrics in metrics pipeline; retention 90d. Owner: Jon. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- [ ] Build Dashboard draft (compact) and run 1-on-1 with oncall rota for feedback. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2026-03-08.

Notes to self / operators:
- Keep session window small for p50/p95 calculations (defaults: 30s sliding for session-level p50, 5m for p95 rollup).
- When capturing trace ids in dashboards, truncate for display but store full id for API lookup.
- Use linked_artifacts above for design doc and PRs.

Appendix: quick instrumentation checklist
- add session_id attr (string) to router runtime span
- increment model_fanout_count counter on every backend call
- emit kvcache_hit boolean tag on request end
- emit session-level aggregate event once per session end or every N requests

Unresolved: how to fairly attribute shared kv-cache to multiple tenants when prefetched keys are cold? Put on backlog for capacity/cost workshop.

Feedback welcome — drop notes on the Confluence page or ping #observability on Slack.
